max_checkpoints.description:
Optional cap on the total number of successful checkpoints this policy will take before it
auto-disables. `None` (the field absent) means run indefinitely; when present it must be
`> 0` (validated at policy creation — a `<= 0` value is rejected with a 400, not stored).
Lets the UI express e.g. "4 checkpoints/day for 7 days" as interval=21600, max_checkpoints=28.

`i32` (not `u32`) on purpose: the enforcement query casts this JSONB value to a Postgres
`int` range for comparison. Keeping the type in `i32` range means an oversized value is
rejected at deserialization (clean 400) rather than stored and then blowing up the cap
query. The query itself casts to `bigint` defensively. Matches the cedana-ui type.

post.description:
Worker pods are resolved AUTHORITATIVELY server-side by the Dynamo labels the
operator stamps on each pod — `nvidia.com/dynamo-graph-deployment-name` (exact
match on the DGD name) and `nvidia.com/dynamo-component` (to exclude the
Frontend) — scoped to the cluster via `pod_relations` and the namespace. This
replaces the previous client-side `pod_name.startsWith(deployment)` heuristic,
which could checkpoint a *different* deployment's workers when two DGDs shared
a name prefix in the same namespace (e.g. `vllm-agg` vs `vllm-agg-cedana`).
